Elaine — thanks, this is a great starting point. I've sketched a pragmatic tranche-based MAP that balances Aurora's need for a fast pilot with Redwood's procurement lead times. High level:

- Tranche 0 (evaluation): short-term staging capacity on shared infra (no long lead time) — evaluation window 2 weeks.
- Tranche 1 (initial committed pool): sign commitment by Aug 20 -> hardware lead time to reserve capacity for Sep 10 availability.
- Tranche 2 (scale/steady-state): optional additional commit by Oct 15 for Nov/Dec provisioning.

Sizing guidance based on your 25 QPS target and 512-token median: we estimate a starting pool of 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized model profile) to hit the pilot SLOs with room for burst. For steady-state production at 95th percentile throughput with redundancy, plan 24 x A100-equivalents (or smaller number of next-gen cards depending on model sizing). I'll attach a short tranche options deck and an acceptance checklist.

Key dates I recommend we include in the MAP:
- 2026-08-09: evaluation kickoff (staging token/data prep)
- 2026-08-23: pilot validation window begins
- 2026-09-06: pilot close & acceptance decision
- 2026-09-10: Tranche 1 pool live (if commit reached by 2026-08-20)
- 2026-10-15: Tranche 2 commit cutoff for Nov provisioning

I'll also add clear owners: Redwood SE for model/latency validation (Monica), Redwood Delivery for provisioning (Marissa), Aurora Platform (Josh) for integration testing, Aurora Procurement for PO windows.

Attachments: redwood-tranche-options.pdf, deployment-acceptance-criteria.md.

If that looks reasonable I can fold this into a formatted MAP PDF for signature. Want me to include a short procurement checklist for your PO team (PO template, billing contacts, SLA appendix)?

Thanks,
